_doc: Lever cards (gluon), keyed bound_class -> lever. Read them yourself: the profile ranks the bucket, keep only levers whose gate holds and whose arch/isa/version availability is satisfied. Numeric cutoffs live in thresholds.json (not here); this file = availability + applicability + the gating laws. version_gate/probe resolve at RUNTIME (probe-per-build; never baked to a container). Recipe cards additionally carry api_ref (the L2 <dsl>/*-reference.md#section whose API the lever code calls); read it before applying the lever and cite it in your round record; references_read before a recipe edit. onboarding[] = the intro/basic-writing docs the gate (A0) requires be read ONCE before the first authoring round (the pack entry `skill.md ## Mechanism` names the onboarding layer); everything after stays lazy-loaded. Layout-sensitive matrix-core cards carry layout_gen (a scripts/layout_facts.py command that GENERATES the MFMA operand layout/dims/GPR facts up front, replacing a compile-and-see probe).
_arch_policy: arch_availability values: yes | no | tier-b | partial | probe. An arch NOT listed in a card defaults to 'probe' (NOT 'yes') — an unverified arch must be probed, never silently recommended. gfx1250 (CDNA5/MI450) and gfx1201/gfx1100 (RDNA) are WMMA/TDM, NOT MFMA: any card with isa_gate MFMA/scaled-MFMA does not apply there -- check isa.mfma/scaled_mfma is false, so MFMA-only levers do not leak onto a WMMA arch. WMMA equivalents are probe/author (capability-matrix.md gfx1250/gfx1201 rows).

gating_laws.when: in-band scheduling hints (sched_group_barrier / reorder) applied to a fused multi-purpose loop body
gating_laws.effect: the hints only reorder WITHIN one scheduling region, so on a fused matmul1 + epilogue-reduction + matmul2 body they cannot reach the reference schedule density (they stall on the cross-region operand/sync drains); split the body into separate scheduling regions and defer the epilogue one tile FIRST, then the in-region hints pay

gating_laws.when: a compiler-realized lever (instruction-interleave / register-allocation / post-asm peephole) is applied WITHOUT the paired source structure already written
gating_laws.effect: the pass EXPLOITS author-engineered independence + register headroom, it does not CREATE them; without independent AC/LR/DOT + a fitting register budget the knob is neutral (or asserts / regresses). A compiler ceiling is valid ONLY after IR shows the structure IS correct yet the pass still clumps/spills — else it is a kernel-structure bug, not a compiler miss. A source enabler + its paired compiler lever are ONE coupled win (the enabling-step exception): the source step (3-stage prefetch / N-slice) may be flat/negative alone and only nets out once the compiler lever (scheduling / the AGPR hint) lands.

manual_pipeline_prefetch.note: THE CLIMB DEFAULT on the Gluon path, and the base the other scheduling models sit on: hand-build the CROSS-ITERATION double-buffer (store-next at loop bottom / load-current at top). Decide groups_per_stage FIRST -- wait_group(N) counts COMMIT GROUPS, N = groups_per_stage * stages_in_flight -- and note N is a static attribute that must reduce to a Python int at trace time, which is why a dynamic loop branches between two literals. Production (429 gfx950 Gluon kernels, triton 3.8): 228 files / 797 commit_group sites; instruction scheduling layers on top in 91, hand-rolled wave priority in 13 of 13. NEVER take the disableSched path (occupancy cliff), and an IN-ITERATION store->barrier->read staging REGRESSES on a 2-wave kernel. gfx942 is 'partial': async_copy lowers there only at 32-bit per thread with a contiguous-tiling BlockedLayout. EXCLUSIVE with reinject_ttgir_pipeliner in the SAME loop. COUNTER-WEIGHT: in a measured gfx950 campaign every overlap mechanism lost to a plain synchronous retiling -- read a pipeline regression as a layout question first.

In-band knobs exist in some LLVM but availability + valid strings are probe-per-build; manual AC/LR/DOT interleave is the portable fallback. PREREQUISITE is the gating_law above: satisfy it BEFORE sweeping. The WALL, and the exit for when the schedule is NOT the problem, are both computable before any sweep -- tile-programming/llir-codesign.md ## Attention: the co-execution budget and ## When the schedule is not the problem. mem_stage_phase_pacing.verify: in-loop matrix-issue efficiency per SIMD up while the instruction inventory is UNCHANGED (that is the tell it is a phase effect); the region head's 3-source vector block no longer coincides with the other wave's LDS-return burst in an instruction trace
mem_stage_phase_pacing.probe: sweep the small integer count exhaustively (0..4) -- the response is NOT monotone, so bisection misleads; keep the winner per kernel, and re-sweep after any change to the stage split
mem_stage_phase_pacing.note: A PHASE lever, not a quantity lever, and the only one on this list that deliberately ADDS idle cycles. Issuing in the same cycle is necessary for two instructions to overlap but not sufficient: the register file sits behind both issue ports, so a 3-source vector op (fused-multiply-add, a 3-input max) and an arriving LDS return contend for ports. A compute region puts its 3-source work exactly where the collision is worst, because a reduction is first in dependency order and the scheduler has nowhere else to put it. Padding the head of the MEMORY stage shifts that wave's reads later so they arrive past the 3-source block and land on cheaper work instead -- the kernel is unchanged, only the phase relationship between the two waves moves. COMPANION LEVER from the opposite end: remove the third source (fold a scale into an operand loaded once upstream so a fused op becomes a plain subtract), verified by counting 3-source vector ops in the loop body. DO NOT confuse with the compiler-inserted hazard nop: that one reads as exposed fixed-latency and is answered with unroll/occupancy, and reorder cannot create slack there (hardware/bound-class-signals.md ## Stall-reason → lever).

warp_pipeline_schedule.kernel_rules: launch enough warps and CONFIRM 2 waves/SIMD (else one issue stream, the schedule degenerates); the mem stage gets the HIGHER priority (warp_pipeline_stage('mem', priority=1) vs ('mfma', priority=0)) so its address VALU keeps issuing under the compute group; keep wait_group / fences OUT of the compute stage — resolve LDS hazards a full stage early (S-1 -> S+1, because one group runs a stage behind); a redundant lgkmcnt(0)+s_barrier landing inside the compute stage fragments MFMA issue — elide it (load_shared_relaxed or per-quadrant LDS allocs), gated by the determinism race-test

warp_pipeline_schedule.note: route=wave-pingpong: the inter_wave scheduling MODEL -- the intelligence is in the KERNEL wave structure, not the compiler. Runs on STOCK Triton (no plugins, no env, no rebuild; only llvm_fn_attrs=amdgpu-agpr-alloc=0,0). GLUON-ONLY BY CONSTRUCTION: add_warp_pipeline appears exactly once in the AMD backend, inside gluon_to_ttgir, so a marker from plain Triton is never grouped -- plain's analog is the automatic add_block_pingpong, which you do not place. THREE COMPILE-TIME CONSTRAINTS: a stage region may contain NO barrier, NO wait and NO loop, and the markers must produce at least TWO stages (barriers are legal BETWEEN stages). The no-wait rule is what makes layering this over an authored ring hard, and why 5 of the 8 production files that use it carry no commit_group at all; for priority control inside a body that has waits, bare s_setprio via inline asm is the route (13 production files, usually but not always on top of a ring). NOT tagged occupancy_gates_latency: it REQUIRES 2 waves/SIMD as a precondition. NVIDIA analog = warp specialization, which gfx950 cannot reach (warp_specialize hard-errors: gfx1250 only).

grid_axis_defuse.note: Reverse of kernel fusion: split a fused kernel by output / parallel axis into separate dispatches so each output's reduction becomes CLEAN and the atomic/RMW combine disappears (e.g. attention-bwd fused -> separate dkdv and dq kernels). See also the `P0 (defuse-by-parallel-axis)` section of the host-dispatch-strategies page in the hip / flydsl / cuda / cutedsl packs (an external pack page: the Triton-family packs, this one included, do not ship it, so treat this note as the whole account here). Distinct from split_k / materialize (those SPLIT ONE reduction into partials + a combine kernel); defuse re-picks the parallel axis so DIFFERENT outputs each land clean. The fused<->split call is symmetric — floor-probe both sides before committing; do not blindly defuse (you lose the fused form's data reuse) nor blindly fuse (you take on atomic contention).

reuse_shared_operand_load.note: First-principles NOVEL lever (not a base card): when memory-bound with a provably duplicated per-iter load of a shared operand, try fetching it once and reusing it. Illustrates the card-is-a-floor-not-a-ceiling principle: reason from the profile and probe an off-card direction. NCU register-vs-shared / data-reuse analog: reuse a loaded operand from registers/shared instead of re-fetching it.

single_barrier_double_buffer.note: Fold the redundant end-of-loop barrier into the top barrier so ONE full sync per K-tile guarantees both current-data-ready and prev-reads-done (2 -> 1 barrier/tile). Register-neutral. GATE ON criticality: a barrier-removal floor probe must show the barrier is on the critical path; if removing it leaves the time unchanged the bound is issue-rate (reduce_lds_read_issue_rate) or elsewhere, not over-sync. NCU barrier-stall analog: avoid unnecessary barriers; divergence before a barrier inflates the wait.
